question.text: The length of the second hand of a clock is 2.0 cm. Determine the average speed along with the magnitude of the average velocity of its tip over a time interval of 15 s.
conditions: length of second hand r = 2.0 cm
second hand completes one full rotation in 60 s with constant angular speed

solution.approach: The tip moves at constant speed around a circle of radius 2.0 cm; find the quarter-turn distance for speed and the chord length for velocity.

steps.text: The second hand's tip moves on a circle of radius 2.0 cm and completes one full turn in 60 s.
In 15 s the tip sweeps a quarter turn, so the distance travelled is a quarter of the circumference.
Average speed is this distance divided by the time.
The displacement is the straight chord between the start point and the point a quarter turn later, which are 90° apart on the circle.
Average velocity magnitude is this displacement divided by the time.
steps.why_this_step: Displacement is the straight-line chord, which is shorter than the curved arc distance.

final_answer.value: average speed ≈ 0.21 cm/s (π/15 cm/s); average velocity magnitude ≈ 0.19 cm/s (2√2/15 cm/s)

common_mistakes.text: Using the full circumference 4π cm for the 15 s interval instead of the quarter-turn distance π cm, giving an average speed of about 0.84 cm/s.
Treating the arc distance and the chord displacement as the same length, giving 0.21 cm/s for both average speed and average velocity.
